notes:
Summary: Valence is a mid-to-large enterprise search vendor migrating core ranking and semantic-search pipelines to dedicated inference to guarantee customer SLAs. They've run initial hosted POCs (Jan-Feb) and want a Dedicated contract with throughput guarantees and a predictable burst policy.

Key ask (from CTO & infra lead):
- Minimum sustained tokens/sec guarantee measured at gateway (not per-GPU) for 95% of operating hours. They proposed a baseline of 12,000 tok/s sustained across multi-region serving for core rerank path.
- Concurrency caps: want per-tenant concurrency isolation with soft limit 250 concurrent requests and hard cap 500; also request per-route isolation for reranking and chat.
- Burst policy: allow short bursts up to 3x baseline for up to 10 minutes per hour without immediate overage, with throttling model thereafter. Want a burst bucket semantics rather than immediate token billing.
- Latency SLOs: p95 generation latency target for 256-token responses <= 180ms; p99 < 450ms. Prefers p95 per-route and p99 at account-level.
- Reserved GPU sizing: infra team expects 8x A100-ish equivalents (or 16x A5000-style for cost tradeoff) behind autoscaler; want pre-warmed KV cache pools to avoid cold starts.
- Availability: target 99.9% up-time for Dedicated runtime, with credit-backed SLA and a rollback path to hosted fallbacks during regional outages.

Notes from meetings: 
- "We need determinism during peak trading windows — spikes are predictable and costly." — CTO (2026-02-18).
- SE ran baseline: internal benchmark with 6k tok/s sustained on 4xA100; projection to hit Valence target requires ~8xA100 with continuous batching and cache warmers.
- They dislike per-token burst overage unpredictability; ask for hybrid model: committed baseline + predictable burst allotment per month.

Technical/ops concerns called out: 
- Measurement: require a canonical measurement method (tokens/sec at API ingress, 1-minute sliding window, 95th percentile) and shared telemetry. Redwood must expose token-metering hooks and raw traces for audit.
- Concurrency isolation: request node-level tenancy or soft quota enforcement per-customer to prevent noisy neighbor.
- Cache warming: explicit SLA that KV cache hit-rate will be maintained during redeploys or warm-starts; otherwise have a brief performance penalty credit.
- Autoscale ramp: need documented autoscale ramp-up time and guaranteed warm capacity for known peak windows (calendar-driven bursts).

Commercial asks: 
- Want a 12-month reserved commitment with monthly billing and defined overage pricing capped at +25% of committed spend for predictable finance.
- Request a clause for performance credits if sustained throughput drops below guaranteed baseline for >30 mins in a rolling 24h window.

POC / Runbook plan:
- Week 0: sign MSA + NDA addendum for model licensing.
- Week 1-2: Redwood SE to run deterministic load tests (Valence test harness) to validate tokens/sec and latency curves with proposed model variants.
- Week 3: Joint runbook: capacity plan, autoscale policy, KV cache warming scripts, escalation playbook.
- Milestone: acceptance = 5 consecutive business days meeting min tokens/sec at the agreed latency SLO.

Direct links: deck + capacity spreadsheet in Drive (see linked_drive_docs). Fireflies contains call transcripts (linked_fireflies).

Open legal points: penalty computation formula (credit %), termination rights if sustained under-provisioning, data residency appendices for EU customers.

Sales notes (short):
- Champion: CTO (Marcus Lee). Procurement lead: Sarah Nguyen. Infra lead: Daniel Park.
- Risk: legal pushback on SLA credits; finance wants capped overage.
- Win criteria: signed 12mo commit + first-month reserved capacity payment.
